recipes.name: Baked Lentils with Cheese
ingredients_raw: 2 large carrots, cut into 1/2 inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Mix water, lentils, stewed tomatoes, onions, garlic, salt, pepper, marjoram, sage, thyme, and bay leaf together in a 3-quart casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered, in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.
Stir in carrots and celery; cover and continue to bake until lentils and vegetables are tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir in bell pepper, then sprinkle Cheddar over top. Bake, uncovered, until cheese has melted, about 5 more minutes. Remove bay leaf before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Lentils with Cheese
raw_recipe.description: My mom used to make me these cheesy lentils when I was a teenage vegetarian. It’s still one of my favorite dishes!

review.reviewBody: This recipe is from the More with Less cookbook - I was asking my mom for the recipe she used to make and she pointed me to this cookbook. It's really tasty and healthy.

I chose this recipe because we have started a new lifestyle change - cutting out highly processed foods and adding more highly nutritious foods to our diet. So I was looking for something new we'd never had. I did make some changes to this recipe. First I used homemade vegetable stock in place of the water and ended up using 3 cups total. I used a mixture of red & brown lentils because the recipe didn't specify. I omitted the marjoram & sage because I didn't have them. I used 1 tsp minced garlic from a jar and a mixture of red/green/yellow peppers because that's what I had. I sautéed the onion, carrots, celery, and green peppers for about 5 minutes in a little olive oil for added flavor. I also didn't read the directions thoroughly and ended up combining everything but the cheese in the pan. I baked it for 30 minutes at 350 and checked it, the liquid was gone (which is why I added another cup as stated above for a total of 3 cups) at this point I turned my oven up to 400 covered with foil and baked an additional 45-55 minutes, checking a few times for doneness. I also added onion powder, garlic powder, and oregano - to taste because it was too bland for my tastes. I did not bake it with the cheese it melted without putting it back in the oven. This isn't a dish I will cook every week, but it changes things up and I would make it again.

I've made this once and will be making it again today but will change the method. The flavors were wonderful, but the oven method didn't work well for me. So, today, my plan is to soften the vegetables (onion, carrot, celery, pepper) in olive oil on the stovetop, then add the stewed tomatoes, water, lentils, and seasonings, and leave on a low flame until the lentils have softened. I think it'll be quicker and more thoroughly and reliably cooked than in the oven. I also plan on using feta rather than cheddar as well as a few tablespoons of fresh oregano.

This recipe came from a vegetarian cookbook from the 70s or early 80s and has been one of my staples, whenever looking for a meatless dish. My husband, an ardent meat-etarian, loves it. Over the years I've made lots of changes, depending on what vegetables I have on hand. Leeks, mushrooms, different kinds of peppers, celery root, and different herbs, each giving a unique twist. It becomes an excellent base for whatever flavours you crave. I generally use chicken or vegetable broth instead of water. I also sometimes sauté the veg first to develop a bit more flavour, but I do like the way the recipe suggests you add the veg, too, which helps maintain their original shape. Also I've used different kinds of cheese. Swiss gives it a nutty taste. Love this recipe.

I made some minor changes: 10 oz fresh tomato instead of canned, a second stalk of celery, red bell pepper instead of green, and used 1.25 C cheddar and .25 C feta (ran out of cheddar). This is really good. Even hubby liked it, which is rare for a lentil dish!

The first time i made this, I cheated and used canned lentils. Just sautéed the Vegetables then mixed it all and put it in a casserole and topped with cheese. It was really good! This time I followed the recipe and used dried lentils. It came out dry and not as tasty.

I have made this dish for years and my husband and 2 kids love it, despite the fact that they don't really care for beans. I keep it covered throughout the oven time until ready for the cheese. I add more celery because I love cooked celery. I don't add the green pepper at all. As mentioned by the person who shared the recipe, this is a great dish to serve when you have folks in the crowd who are vegetarian. Not for vegans, of course, due to cheese.

This is a delicious dish. I did not have some of the spices so I added garlic powder, thyme and Italian spice. I think the next time I make this I will use a different cheese like gruyere. I found the cheddar too stringy. I think the cooking time wss little long. I perfere the veggies to be crunchy.

My super picky kids, all four of them are this and told me we can have this for dinner all the time. I did blend the veggies in my nutribullet so they couldn't see them but otherwise followed it to the letter. Will have this again.

Wow, I was looking for an easy side to use up some lentils and had everything on hand for this delicious treat. I did mix a little mozzarella cheese with the cheddar. Will make this again and recommend highly, thank you Tiffany!

I liked this okay, but I found that it needed a lot more seasoning. I used Rotel tomatoes, twice as much garlic than called for, and a healthy dash of cayenne pepper, but still found the flavor overwhelmed by the cheese (of which I only used half of what was called for). This is not a bad dish, but you really have to season to your tastes. I think siracha hot sauce would be really good in it, but I put that on everything as it is.

I made this, but made several changes. I boiled the dried lentils for a few minutes and let them sit covered for 45 min. I sautéed the onions, sweet peppers, garlic, celery first. Then added the a can of diced tomatoes to the mixture. Cooked the mixture at 350 deg. For 35 min uncovered. Then added 1 cup salsa and 1 cup sharp cheddar to the top and baked at 375 for 15 minutes. Delicious!
This is what I like to call a do-over! It goes into my category of recipes that I will definitely make again! Yum!!!
This is from the old vegetarian times cookbook. One of my faves too.
I was looking for a high protein vegetarian meal (I eat cheese). This was it! Amazing how good it was and that the lentils cooked. Since it makes so much, I brought it to work and they loved it!

I made this recipe for my 14 month old and he loved it. I also enjoyed it. I did not have celery so I suspect the flavor could only get better. I also added the cheese to soon. I will make this again. Great as a main dish or side dish.
So savory and delicious! Very filling too.
A great side dish when looking for something different.

What a lovely way to have lentil stew! This was so comforting on a cold winter night and I truly enjoyed it. I did omit the green pepper as I am not really a fan of it. Otherwise I made it as written.

A few years ago, when I had an 8-month-old baby and was pregnant with another, I came home from work to this incredible dish cooking in the oven. My mother-in-law had made it for my birthday dinner. I ate it like there was no tomorrow, and every time I make it, I can't believe how delicious something this healthy can be. It's one of my husband's and my very favorite foods.
